name: Una Roman
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember finding a whole neighborhood missing from a traffic count.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Una by a small Wednesday habit. Una watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I am counting how many people stop to help. The official survey only counts the late vans.
appearance: Una has a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Una looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Una loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Una remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To measure how long real people spent helping.
family: Duncan Woods is Una’s cousin raised in the same household. Una makes the call. Duncan is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The free fringe*, Duncan says, “I am paid by the cut. I'm asking the owner to count time spent with a customer who keeps their hair.”
connections: Darcy Osei. A rescued cart's regulars become the first people counted in the help survey.
